avoid_when: Your data is already a grid
data_needs: A group column and an order in each group
about.example: Households with 3 trips and 1 trip become a 2 by 3 grid with two empty cells.
outputs: A grid of groups by position, and a mask of the real cells
about.summary_plain: Puts the rows of each group side by side in a grid. It fills short groups with gaps and marks the gaps as missing.
about.title: Put groups side by side
use_when: A model needs a grid of groups by position, such as households by trip

DimPolicy.description: What may happen to a dim's coordinates at score time.
DimPolicy.title: DimPolicy

group.description: Variable along the rows naming each row's group
group.title: Group

group_dim.description: Name of the outer dim (existing or new)
group_dim.title: Group Dim

mask_var.description: Name of the boolean validity mask to add
mask_var.title: Mask Var

vars.description: Every other variable on the rows
vars.title: Vars

within_dim.description: Name of the new position dim
within_dim.title: Within Dim

steps.summary: Long ragged data to padded form with a mask
steps.summary_plain: Lines up each group's rows side by side, padding short groups

assumptions: The drift continues at the same rate into the future
avoid_when: The trend changes direction frequently (use a flexible trend model)
data_needs: A regular date column
about.example: Week 1 gets 0, week 52 gets 1, and week 104 gets 2.
outputs: A trend column (optionally curved)
about.summary_plain: Adds a column that counts up over time, so a model can show a steady increase or decrease.
about.title: Steady drift over time
use_when: Your result increases or decreases steadily

power.description: Polynomial power of the scaled trend
power.title: Power

scale_to_fit.description: Scale so the fitted range maps to [0, 1] (forecasts continue past 1)
scale_to_fit.title: Scale To Fit

steps.summary: Polynomial time trend
steps.summary_plain: Adds a steady upward or downward drift over time

assumptions: The parts of each combined label are known
avoid_when: No step stacked the dimensions
data_needs: A dimension that a stack step made
about.example: 12 market-product cells become 3 markets by 4 products.
outputs: The original dimensions
about.summary_plain: Divides a combined dimension back into its parts. For example, market-product cells become markets and products again.
about.title: Split a combined dimension
use_when: You stacked dimensions in an earlier step and you need the grid again

steps.summary: Unstack a dim into several
steps.summary_plain: Splits a combined dimension back into its parts
